properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar, using reflow2 as a project brain at work, relayed by Anthony 2026-09-21. STILL OPEN.

THE REPORT, IN HIS TERMS. He is ingesting the contents of several existing project repositories. Each component gets a unique TEXT NAME. His export is past 50,000 lines and he estimates he is about a quarter of the way through. Duplicate components get created, and his words are that reflow2 "had no way to efficiently query what was already in the graph". His workplace is billed per token rather than on a subscription, and he measured roughly $70 in one day. He also said the effort of going through all the code and documentation himself is substantial, which is a separate cost and not a token cost.

THE PART HE FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN, AND IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING PART. Anthony relayed that his components have a unique PATH, and that he is assigning the path to the nodes as a sort of unique identifier — and said plainly that this part does not make complete sense to him. So it is second-hand and unconfirmed. Read as written, it is a person reaching for a NATURAL KEY: something about the real-world thing that is already unique, so two writes about one thing collide instead of multiplying.

WHY A TEXT NAME MAKES DUPLICATES INEVITABLE AT THIS SCALE, stated as the shape of the problem rather than as a cause nobody measured: a name is chosen by whoever is writing, and on the tenth day of ingesting the tenth repository the same component is named slightly differently. The near-match guard catches some of that, and `fact:defect-ingest-writes-duplicates-that-heal-then-merges` measured what the scorer does at the edges — token_sort_ratio over names only, scoring 81-85 on semantically unrelated nodes. A path does not have that problem, because it is not a description.

THE OPTIONS, in no order, and none of them chosen.

(a) A BULK EXISTENCE CHECK. One call that takes many candidate keys and answers which already exist, with a tiny reply — ids and nothing else. Today an agent either asks per node, which is N round trips, or reads a scan into context, which is what costs the money. CHEAP: it is a read against an index the store already has. THE COUNTER: it only helps if the agent HAS keys to ask about, which is option (b)'s question; asked with names it inherits the same ambiguity.

(b) A NATURAL KEY ON THE NODE. Let a node carry the identifier the real world already gives it — a repository path, a fully qualified module name, a document URI — and make a second write to the same key an update rather than a new node. CHEAP: duplicates stop being something to detect, because they stop being writable. THE COUNTER, and it is the strong one: `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` decided reflow2's systems are FUNCTIONAL and not the file tree. A path is a fact about the repository. Keying a Component on a path quietly re-decides that, and the wrong altitude is harder to fix than an empty graph because it looks finished. The narrower form that may survive it is the one `dec:idea-mechanical-code-structure-ingest` already names: key the ARTIFACT layer on the path, because there the identity genuinely IS the file, and leave Components alone.

(c) SPEND THE MODEL ONLY ON WHAT THE FILE CANNOT SAY. Already open as `dec:idea-mechanical-code-structure-ingest`: extract the structural half mechanically and deterministically, and reserve the agent for intent. His $70 a day is the first COST measurement this project has for that idea, and cost was not among the arguments recorded for it.

(d) NOTHING NEW — the near-match guard already refuses a duplicate at the constructor. THE COUNTER: it refuses one at a time, after the agent has already composed and sent the node, so it saves the graph and not the tokens; and at 50,000 lines the population it is matching against is far past what a name-similarity score was measured to be sound on.

(e) A CLIENT-SIDE MANIFEST. The ingesting agent keeps its own list of what it has written and consults that instead of the graph. CHEAP and requires nothing from reflow2. THE COUNTER: it is wrong across sessions and wrong across two people, which is exactly the case he is in, and it puts the design's memory somewhere the design cannot read — the thing this project keeps deciding against.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN AND WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER. Nobody here has measured where his $70 actually goes. Reading source and documents into context to understand them is irreducible and may be most of it; re-reading the graph to check for duplicates may be a little of it. Those two have opposite fixes, and the cheapest next move is to find out which it is rather than to build for the guess.
properties.name: OPEN — how does an agent ingesting a large repository find out what the graph already holds, cheaply enough to ask before every node it writes?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea rather than as intent because the owner has not chosen, and because the two most promising options pull against an accepted decision (dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition) that must be answered rather than stepped around. Kept as one question with options rather than split, because (a) and (b) are alternative answers to the same thing and half-answering it would be worse than leaving it open. The uncertainty in the path detail is recorded as uncertainty: it arrived second-hand and the relayer said so.
